run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T09:35:43Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on frontend-proxy is caused by HTTP 504 gateway timeouts on GET /api/recommendations. The 15s that frontend-proxy waits is spent inside the frontend's gRPC call to recommendation (grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations = 15.34s of a 15.34s frontend request in the fetched 504 trace), while recommendation's own downstream product-catalog calls are sub-millisecond. The deepest supported cause is that the recommendation pod (recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv, node i-07fdfccf76e0651ab) became CPU-quota starved: its container CPU limit is 0.1 core and its CFS throttling ratio jumped from ~5% (09:10-09:32Z) to 86-98% at 09:36-09:47Z, with CPU usage rising ~8x at the same time, while request rate to it was flat (~0.78-0.88 spans/s through 09:34:43Z) and then collapsed to 0 as its own telemetry stopped after ~09:37Z. The frontend's p95 span latency rose from ~196-267ms (baseline 09:15-09:31Z) to 988ms (09:35Z) and 4688ms (09:40Z), then requests exceeded the proxy's 15s timeout and frontend-proxy ingress spans began returning 504 with otel.status_code ERROR, growing to ~59 errors per 735s by 09:44Z. product-catalog (34µs-1ms per call), node-level CPU (host ~90% idle) and frontend/frontend-proxy CPU throttling (flat ~20-27% / ~3-5%) were checked and do not explain it. What made recommendation's CPU demand rise ~8x at constant load is not observable with the available telemetry and remains an open hypothesis/gap.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's error spans are confined to span_name "ingress": its 735s-window increase went from 0 before 09:12Z to ~1.1 at 09:14Z, ~9.2 at 09:35Z, ~42.9 at 09:39Z and ~59.4 at 09:44Z; the matching "router frontend egress" span stayed at 0 errors.

Across services, frontend-proxy is the dominant error-span contributor (735s increase 9.2 to 59.4 between 09:35Z and 09:48Z), while ad, fraud-detection and recommendation show only ~1.0-2.0 per 735s and cart, frontend and payment stay at 0.

The frontend-proxy error spans are HTTP 504 responses of exactly ~15,000,000µs with otel.status_code ERROR; the paired "router frontend egress" span carries error="true" and http.status_code "0", i.e. no upstream response status was received.
frontend-proxy access logs show "504 UT response_timeout" only for GET /api/recommendations, with upstream response time 14999-15001ms, continuously from 09:37:00Z through 09:41:08Z.

In the whole trace of one 504 (trace 3761ca9dd7eb387d96ebefddcd0680f0, ~09:41:11Z) the frontend server span GET /api/recommendations is 15,342,201µs and its child grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations client span is 15,338,669µs (rpc.grpc.status_code 0), while the product-catalog ListProducts span inside that call is 34µs and starts ~12.3s after the request began.

In five earlier >5s frontend traces (09:42:17Z-09:42:35Z), GET /api/recommendations took 5.25-6.63s and the ListRecommendations client span accounted for 5.14-6.51s, while product-catalog spans stayed at 36µs-116ms; no span from the recommendation service appears in those traces.

frontend span-latency p95 was 196-267ms from 09:15Z to ~09:31Z (baseline) and then rose to 988ms at 09:35Z and 4,688ms at 09:40Z; recommendation's p95 over the same buckets was 49-193ms and became uncomputable (NaN) in the 09:45Z bucket.

The recommendation pod's CFS throttling ratio rose from ~0.05 (09:10:43Z-09:32:43Z) to 0.516 at 09:34:43Z, 0.856 at 09:36:43Z and ~0.96-0.98 from 09:38:43Z to 09:47:43Z, while frontend (0.20-0.27) and product-catalog (0.18-0.22) stayed flat.

Only recommendation crossed 0.2 throttling in the later part of the window: it is at 0.70 (09:36:43Z), 0.97 (09:38:43Z) and 0.98 (09:43:43Z), whereas cart, frontend, postgresql and product-catalog remain 0.20-0.29 across the window.

Recommendation container CPU usage rose from ~0.023-0.026 cores (09:10Z-09:32Z) to 0.094 (09:34:43Z), 0.163 (09:36:43Z) and ~0.19 thereafter, while frontend (~0.08-0.09), frontend-proxy (~0.022-0.024) and product-catalog (~0.013-0.016) were unchanged.
The recommendation container's CPU limit is 0.1 core (resource cpu, unit core); frontend's is 0.1 and frontend-proxy's is 0.03.

Request rate to recommendation did not rise before the CPU spike: its ListRecommendations/ListProducts/get_product_list span rates were 0.57-1.03 per second from 09:12:43Z through 09:34:43Z, then 0.289 at 09:36:43Z and 0 from 09:38:43Z onward.

recommendation's own span medians were healthy before its telemetry stopped: /oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations p50 1.64-1.86ms, /oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts 1.13-1.18ms and get_product_list 1.23-1.28ms; all recommendation span series are NaN in the 09:40Z and 09:45Z buckets, and a /flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream span shows p50 15000ms in two buckets.

The recommendation container keeps logging "Receive ListRecommendations for product ids:[...]" throughout 09:39:24Z-09:40:47Z, i.e. it is still accepting request work after its span metrics stop; the log lines contain no error text.

recommendation's memory working set grew from ~84.4MB (09:10Z-09:34Z) to 99.2MB (09:36:43Z), 106.2MB (09:41:43Z) and 108.9MB (09:46:43Z); frontend-proxy's stayed flat at ~41MB and frontend grew modestly 244MB to 264MB.

recommendation-5f45f75855-htttv is Running with restart count 0 and start time 08:54:20Z, i.e. it was not restarted during the incident; the only pods with restarts are fraud-detection (3 restart count) and flagd.

The only Warning events in otel-demo in the window concern fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-dz8j9 (BackOff restarting failed container at 09:15:31Z, container Started 09:15:46Z); no event mentions the recommendation pod.

The current flagd-config configmap has every fault-injection flag at defaultVariant "off", including recommendationCacheFailure, recommendation-related ad/product flags, paymentFailure and imageSlowLoad.

Host system CPU reported through the collector's system metrics at 09:46Z shows ~0.90 idle and only ~0.076-0.080 user per CPU on the collector host (the node that also runs the recommendation pod), so host CPU was not saturated.

No rpc_client_duration_milliseconds or http_server_request_duration_seconds series exist in this target; the only span metrics available are traces_span_metrics_calls_total and traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket.

Primary causal chain: the recommendation container is pinned at its 0.1-core CPU limit and throttled 86-98% of CFS periods, so each ListRecommendations call now takes seconds; the frontend's request therefore exceeds frontend-proxy's 15s upstream timeout, Envoy answers 504 UT response_timeout, and frontend-proxy's ingress error ratio rises until the RequestErrorRate warning fires.

Why recommendation's CPU demand rose ~8x at a flat request rate (~0.78-0.88 spans/s) is inside the recommendation process: the candidates supported only circumstantially are GC/allocator thrash accompanying the +24MB working-set growth and an internal busy path; the recommendation logs contain no error text and its pre-failure span medians (1.6-1.9ms) show no downstream dependency problem.

A second, much smaller error source exists on the same proxy: the earlier log slice contains "503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}" for GET /api/cart at 09:25:44Z and GET /api/products/66VCHSJNUP at 09:29:05Z, which predate the recommendation CPU spike and are not explained by it.

product-catalog was checked and looks healthy: in the 504 trace its ListProducts span is 34µs with rpc.grpc.status_code 0, and in the slow frontend traces its server spans are 36-902µs (one 107µs) while the frontend's cached-then-fetched GetProduct client spans are 36µs-2.4ms, so the multi-second delay is not created by product-catalog.

frontend and frontend-proxy were checked for their own CPU pressure and show no change: throttling stays 0.20-0.27 for frontend-675fd7b5c5-x7pxv and ~0.03-0.05 for frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-p8qtl after the alert, and frontend's CPU usage is flat at ~0.08-0.09 cores, so their own CPU does not explain the timeout.

Rejected: the latency comes from a slow or failing product-catalog dependency of recommendation — recommendation's own /oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/ListProducts p50 stayed at 1.13-1.18ms up to the point its telemetry ceased, and product-catalog's server spans in the slow traces are 34µs-902µs.

Rejected: node-level CPU saturation on i-07fdfccf76e0651ab — host system CPU on the collector host (which also hosts recommendation) reports ~90% idle and ~0.08 user utilization at 09:46Z, and the recommendation limitation is its own per-cgroup quota (0.1 core).

Rejected as the cause of this alert: the fraud-detection crash loop (BackOff at 09:15:31Z, container restarted 09:15:46Z, restart count 3) — the 504s are exclusively on GET /api/recommendations and fraud-detection is not on that call path; its own error spans are only ~1.0-1.06 per 735s.

Raise the recommendation workload's CPU request/limit above the current 0.1 core (and re-check node headroom), since the pod is pinned at that quota with 86-98% CFS throttling; consider HPA on CPU and an alert on container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods ratio for recommendation.

Profile the recommendation process for the per-request CPU increase it showed at constant request rate, and check why its span export and log output stop after ~09:37Z / 09:40:47Z while it still accepts requests (exporter starvation under throttling is one candidate).

Review whether any flagd flag or recommendation deployment/config was changed around 09:34Z using a change-history source; the current configmap shows all flags off, but runtime flag state and change events were not observable in this Run.

gaps: No change_history integration is available, so no deployment, config or feature-flag change at ~09:34Z can be confirmed or ruled out — this is the main unresolved question about what raised recommendation's CPU demand.

flagd logs could not be read (fetch_pod_logs for flagd-785747d9d9-zsjrc read 0 bytes from all three containers), so the meaning of recommendation's 15000ms /flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream spans and flagd-side behaviour are unverified.

No independent traffic baseline: traces_span_metrics_calls_total has no load-generator series (no_data), and the metric pipeline only starts around 09:10-09:15Z, so the earlier comparison relies on recommendation's own span rate from 09:12Z, not on a longer pre-incident baseline.

recommendation's own spans stop after ~09:37Z, so there is no server-side latency distribution for the period when the 504s were actually occurring; how much of the 15s was queueing versus processing inside recommendation cannot be measured.

The 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started errors on /api/cart (09:25:44Z) and /api/products (09:29:05Z) are observed but unexplained; their total count within the window is unknown because the log read hit the 4MiB limit.
Only the frontend-proxy pod's frontend-proxy container was inspected; the frontend pod's application logs were not read, so any frontend-side error text about the recommendation call is unknown.

fraud-detection's crash loop (restart count 3, BackOff at 09:15:31Z) was only observed at the event/restart level; its own logs and termination reason were not examined and its relation to the two 503 UC errors is unknown.
next_steps: Raise recommendation's CPU limit/request and redeploy, then re-check container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods ratio, frontend /api/recommendations latency and frontend-proxy 504s.
Profile the recommendation process (e.g. py-spy/GC stats) during a reproduction to identify the per-request CPU increase and the +24MB working-set growth.
Check the flagd runtime flag state and its change history, plus any recommendation deployment/config edits around 09:34Z, using a change-history/audit-log source.
Investigate the 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started errors on /api/cart and /api/products separately, reading frontend logs and the full proxy log window past 09:41Z.
